authored_additions: Both programs are agent-authored illustrations of one task: print the single line HELLO and end. They are not recovered historical source.
Not executed: no IBM 7090/7094 FORTRAN II processor, IBSYS/FORTRAN Monitor, or Dartmouth Time-Sharing System emulation was used. No output, compile result or run is claimed.
FORTRAN II listing: PRINT 1 / 1 FORMAT (6H HELLO) / CALL EXIT / END, in card columns (number in 5, statements from column 7). The blank opening the H field is carriage control.
Message HELLO chosen as a neutral minimal message; the later "hello, world" phrase is deliberately not used.
Plain letter O in both listings; the 1964 manuals print code with a slashed O in places.
On-screen dialect labels 'FORTRAN II for the IBM 7090/7094' and 'Dartmouth BASIC, October 1964' are production additions to the ticket copy.

Comparison variant: line bands, a card-column guide (cols 1-5, col 7 onward) and two captions ('4 statements' / '2 statements' plus one explanatory sentence each). Code size and position are unchanged.
Job control cards (FORTRAN) and terminal commands such as RUN (BASIC) are outside both listings.
